query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Doping a LaFe13-xCoxSi1 compound with a small amount of boron (0.1 atomic percent) will improve its magnetocaloric properties near room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: LaFe13-xCoxSi1 alloy in a disordered state
generation.conditions: Near room temperature (300 K) and under a magnetic field of 2 Tesla
generation.structural_mediator: Modification of the crystal structure and magnetic exchange interactions
generation.mechanism: The introduction of boron atoms will alter the magnetic anisotropy and exchange interactions, leading to an enhancement of the magnetocaloric effect
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in the isothermal entropy change (ΔS) of 20% relative to the undoped LaFe13-xCoxSi1 alloy
generation.boundary: Magnetic field range: 0-5 Tesla, temperature range: 250-350 K
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in magnetocaloric properties may vary depending on the specific composition and processing conditions of the alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the isothermal entropy change (ΔS) of the doped and undoped LaFe13-xCoxSi1 alloys using a magnetometer and a calorimeter
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured ΔS of the doped alloy is not greater than 15% of the undoped alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

frame.limitation: Current materials have limited magnetocaloric performance
